sample_unit: LLM responses (48 AAOS guideline recommendations x 4 LLMs)

links.outcome: Concordance of LLM treatment recommendations with AAOS clinical practice guidelines
links.effect: 135 responses (70.3%) concordant, 43 (22.4%) indeterminate, 14 (7.3%) discordant; ChatGPT-4 79.2% concordant, Mistral-7B 58.3%; no significant difference across LLMs (P = .12).
links.quote: Overall, 135 responses (70.3%) were concordant, 43 (22.4%) were indeterminate, and 14 (7.3%) were discordant.

links.outcome: Proportion of LLM recommendations with verifiable references or citations
links.effect: Only 20 (10.4%) of recommendations were transparent and provided references with full bibliographic details or links to specific peer-reviewed content.
links.quote: Of all recommendations, only 20 (10.4%) were transparent and provided references with full bibliographic details or links to specific peer-reviewed content to support recommendations.

links.outcome: Whether LLM answers provided traceable supporting sources
links.effect: Only 10.4% of responses gave full references or links; users cannot fully interpret sources of recommendations.
links.quote: Only 10% of responses by LLMs were transparent, precluding users from fully interpreting the sources from which recommendations were provided.

links.outcome: Off-the-shelf LLM clinical competence on guideline-based treatment recommendations
links.effect: More than 1-in-4 recommendations (29.7% indeterminate or discordant) did not reflect CPGs; concordance ranged 58.3% to 79.2% across four LLMs.
links.quote: Among leading commercially available LLMs, more than 1-in-4 recommendations concerning the evaluation and management of rotator cuff and anterior cruciate ligament injuries do not reflect current evidence-based CPGs.

screen.reason: Evaluates the concordance of commercial LLM outputs against clinical practice guidelines for musculoskeletal conditions, without testing a specific deployment practice or guardrail.
